test_title: SSC Selection Post Matric Level Official Paper (Held on: 2 Aug 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
**Select the most appropriate option to replace the underlined word in the given sentence.**

She is so __naïve.__
solution:
Here the correct answer is **Gullible.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate option to replace the underlined word **"naïve"** in the given sentence is** 1) gullible.**
 
• The word **"naïve"** means** having a lack of experience, wisdom, or judgment**. It implies that a person is innocent or simple-minded and may be easily fooled or deceived.
 
 
• Example: He was so **naïve **that he believed everything he was told.
 
 
 
• The word **"gullible"** has a similar meaning to** naïve.** It means** easily deceived or tricked.**
 
 
• Example: She was so **gullible **that she fell for the online scam.
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is Option 1.

**Correct Sentence**__: *She is so __**gullible**__.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2) silly** is not an appropriate replacement for** "naïve"** as it does not convey the same meaning. **Silly **means lacking common sense or being foolish.

 
 
• Example: That was a **silly **mistake to make.
 
 
 
• **Option 3) illiterate **is entirely incorrect as it has no connection to the original meaning. Illiterate means unable to read or write.
 
 
• Example: Many people in the world are **illiterate **and do not have access to education.
 
 
 
• **Option 4) meek **is also not a suitable replacement for "**naïve**" as it does not convey the same meaning. Meek means quiet, gentle, or submissive.
 
 
• Example: She was **meek **and mild-mannered, never wanting to cause any trouble.
